source_title: Lula Secures Historic 4th Term in Brazil, Overturns Runoff Defeat Against Bolsonaro - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term in Brazil, overturning a first-round deficit to defeat Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff with 51.79% of the vote. Lula credited young voters, student demonstrations, and social media outreach for reversing the momentum. Flávio Bolsonaro challenged the outcome and demanded an annulment, claiming extended voting hours affected the result, an argument backed by Donald Trump. However, reports indicated only 35,000 votes were cast during the extension, far fewer than Lula's four-million vote margin. The dispute follows the 27-year prison sentence handed to Jair Bolsonaro in September 2025 for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss. Read More

Uttarakhand Chopper Crash Kills 6, TN Power Row & Madras HC Notice To Sourav Das
A helicopter flying from Badrinath crashed in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, killing all six people on board, including the pilot. Joint search teams comprising the police, SDRF, and the Indian Army recovered the bodies and wreckage near a cliff amid inclement weather and poor visibility. Meanwhile, in Tamil Nadu, a power outage at the Madurai Meenakshi Temple during AIADMK leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami's visit sparked a political storm against the government, with the power minister claiming possible foul play. DMK leaders MK Stalin and Kanimozhi also raised law and order concerns in the state over multiple killings. Additionally, the Madras High Court issued notices to the Centre and Sourav Das over a public interest litigation seeking a probe into his antecedents, cancellation of his passport and Aadhaar card, and the blocking of his social media handles for alleged derogatory remarks against the judiciary.
Govt Clears 100% Flex Fuel Rules; Why Regular Cars Cannot Run On E100
The central government has amended motor vehicle regulations to establish a framework permitting flex-fuel vehicles to run on up to 100 percent ethanol, known as E100. However, conventional petrol vehicles cannot use E85 or E100 fuel, as higher ethanol blends require specialised engines, fuel systems, and sensors. The amendment also increases the weight threshold for light petrol and diesel vehicles from 3,000 kg to 3,500 kg. India is promoting ethanol blending to cut crude oil import dependency and create demand for agricultural produce like sugarcane and maize. Amid the transition, concerns remain among motorists regarding reduced mileage and potential engine wear in vehicles not calibrated for higher blends.
Siang Mega Dam, China Threat & Pasighat Clashes: Why Arunachal Pradesh Is On Boil
India has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh to counterbalance China's construction of a 60,000 MW mega dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet. While the government contends that a large reservoir is vital for water security and managing river flows downstream, local communities are strongly opposing the pre-feasibility surveys. Indigenous Adi youth fear submergence of up to 40 villages, loss of agricultural land, and disruption of their traditional way of life. The escalating standoff turned violent on October 23, resulting in arson at an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, leaving over 40 police personnel injured. Chief Minister Pema Khandu condemned the violence, assuring that the project will advance only through public consensus.
